name: Mont-Saint-Michel and its Bay
description: Rising from vast sandbanks on the border of Normandy and Brittany, Mont-Saint-Michel is a rocky islet crowned by a Benedictine abbey, with a small village huddled beneath its walls. The abbey was built between the 11th and 16th centuries and had to be cleverly engineered to suit its awkward perch. Tides of over 10 metres sweep the bay, so the mount's surroundings change dramatically through the day.
